notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill finds definitions, uses and causes from evidence instead of from the first search hit or a guess. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. Give the model the skill folder without evals/, the sandbox as its working directory, and the prompt. Grade by reading the answer. The skill is written for Windows PowerShell; when the evals run on Linux, say so in the instruction so the model adapts the terminal commands.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
copy evals/sandboxes/<sandbox> to a fresh <work>; for history, run setup.sh inside it once
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system, and for types-q where ty, mypy and pyright are installed

evals.name: same-name-definition
evals.prompt: Where is the load_settings that app/api/server.py calls defined? I need to change its default path.
evals.bait: legacy/config.py also defines load_settings; the used one is reached through a re-export in app/settings/__init__.py
expectations: Answers app/settings/loader.py with the def line, and names DEFAULT_PATH at line 3 as the default
Shows the chain: server.py import, the re-export in app/settings/__init__.py, loader.py
Mentions legacy/config.py only as a different function that server.py does not reach
Does not answer legacy/config.py

evals.name: registry-caller
evals.prompt: Nothing seems to call handle_refund in events/handlers.py. Can I delete it?
evals.bait: it is only called through the HANDLERS table filled by the @handler decorator
expectations: Says no, it is used
Names the @handler("refund") registration and the HANDLERS table in events/registry.py
Names the dispatch in events/dispatch.py and the producer in billing/refunds.py
Does not conclude from a single search for handle_refund(
Lists what was not searched, such as other repositories, or says none with reason

evals.name: reexport-alias
evals.prompt: Where is the Client class that orders/sync.py uses defined?
evals.bait: legacy/client.py has a class named Client; the used one is HttpClient re-exported under the name Client
expectations: Answers shop/api/_http.py, class HttpClient
Shows both re-export hops, including the rename in shop/api/__init__.py
Does not answer legacy/client.py
Uses file and line locations

evals.name: old-code-runs
evals.prompt: I changed src/greeter/core.py to return 'Hello v2', but `python run.py` still prints 'Hello v1'. Why?
evals.bait: run.py inserts vendor_site at the front of sys.path, so a vendored copy is imported
expectations: Asks the interpreter where greeter.core is loaded from, or reads run.py's path setup, rather than rereading the source
Names vendor_site/greeter/core.py as the file that runs
Cites the sys.path.insert(0, ...) line in run.py and the append of src after it
Does not change files without being asked

evals.name: route-by-prefix
evals.bait: the full URL appears nowhere; the path is built from the router prefix, the route path and the include prefix; app/payments/refunds.py has a function named refund
expectations: Answers app/routers/orders.py refund_order
Shows how the path is composed: /api/v1 from app/main.py, /orders from the router, /{order_id}/refund from the decorator
Does not answer app/payments/refunds.py refund

evals.name: orient
evals.prompt: I'm new here. How do I run the tests, and how does the service start?
evals.bait: tests run through nox and skip slow tests; the service starts from the Dockerfile CMD; there is also a CLI entry point; src layout
expectations: Names the nox tests session and that it runs pytest -m 'not slow', from noxfile.py
Names the slow session or the slow marker
Names uvicorn invoicer.web:app from the Dockerfile CMD
Names the invoicer command from [project.scripts]
Notes the src layout and that the package must be installed to import
Does not open source files one by one before the project files

evals.name: type-question
evals.prompt: What exactly does parse_rows in app/rows.py return? I want to annotate it.
evals.bait: no annotations; the answer must come from a checker, not from the name
expectations: Runs at least one type checker with reveal_type in a probe file, not in app/rows.py
Quotes the checker's output line
Reports the type as a list of dict[str, str] or the checker's exact wording
Deletes the probe file afterwards, or says it was left and where
Does not leave reveal_type in project code

evals.name: dotted-string
evals.prompt: Is app.jobs.cleanup.run called from anywhere? A search for run( shows nothing useful.
evals.bait: it is referenced as the string 'app.jobs.cleanup:run' in settings and loaded by importlib in the scheduler
expectations: Finds the string in app/settings.py
Finds the loading in app/scheduler.py (import_module and getattr)
Says it is called by run_all through the settings table
Does not say it is unused

evals.name: fixture-by-name
evals.prompt: Where does db_session in tests/orders/test_refunds.py come from?
evals.bait: two conftest.py files define db_session; the nearest one, tests/orders/conftest.py, wins
expectations: Answers tests/orders/conftest.py
Says tests/conftest.py also defines it and is overridden for tests in tests/orders
Explains pytest passes fixtures by parameter name

evals.name: history-why
evals.prompt: When did MAX_RETRIES in app/net.py change from 5 to 3, and why?
evals.bait: the reason is in the commit message; the last commit to the file is unrelated
expectations: Uses git (log -S, log -L, blame, or log -p) rather than guessing
Names the commit 'Lower retries: the gateway rate limits after 4 attempts (INC-212)', its author Omer Katz
Quotes the reason from the commit message
Does not report the last commit to the file (Add backoff factor) as the change
